questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When riding in groups, riders use hand signals to communicate. If the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, this means the group should stop.

questions.question: Motorcycle windshields:

options.text: Are a good substitute for a face shield.
Are a good substitute for goggles.
Will not protect your eyes from the wind.
Do not protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual tells you about your specific motorcycle.

questions.question: Normally, you should maintain a following distance of:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are bad.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
Keep others from passing you.
Travel to your destination as quickly as possible.
Linger in the blind spots of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to protect your lane and signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Speed up before downshifting safely.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes to ensure that drivers behind you know you are downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting into a lower gear, slow down to a safe speed. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid. Use your brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: Of the following, which is not considered protective clothing?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long pants made of denim
Athletic shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves all protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots or high-top boots with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to weave while you are riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
Tighten your hold on the handle grips and increase your speed to get past the hazard.
Travel in a zigzag motion.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Just relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter, applying the brake when the rider downshifts.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both brakes when either brake lever is applied.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When riding, a cushion of space is helpful to:

options.text: Give you space to react to hazards.
Hide you from other drivers.
Prevent you from avoiding hazards.
Allow you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you space to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT take to improve safety when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights light up the road ahead, and their taillights show if they hit bumps.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's rear brake is operated with the right foot.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, what is usually best?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold both handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
They are caused by faulty ignition systems.
They happen because of passenger distractions.
They occur at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: What does a thorough motorcycle check before riding do?

options.text: Is useless unless a mechanic does it.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should only be done after a ride.
Can help find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: As a motorcycle operator, how can you help others see you?

options.text: Ride with your headlight off.
Wear bright clothing.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Do not use turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothing, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: What kind of footwear should you choose when riding?

options.text: Shoes with long heels.
Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.
Shoes that cover your ankles.
Shoes made from thin materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch on things. Laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding alongside a car?

options.text: It is encouraged.
You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: If the road is slippery.
If there are only a few vehicles on the road.
If the sun is shining.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and the vehicle ahead if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery pavement, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you travel?

options.text: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
At the same speed as you would during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under similar conditions.
On the road shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, travel slower than you would during the day under the same weather and traffic conditions. It is harder to see dangers in the dark, so slowing down helps you avoid hazards.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How should you help a driver merging from an entrance ramp into your lane?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Merge into the next lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are the ones trying to merge.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging drivers space by moving to another lane if you can. They may not see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at intersections. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Never assume drivers see you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: What should you do when preparing to pass a vehicle on the left?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal first, check for traffic, and return to your lane when safe.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver in the lane next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead of them.
A parked car has a person in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing someone who is in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn drivers and pedestrians before you pass them. Use it if you see a driver in a parked car, a pedestrian, or a bicyclist in the street. Do not use it just to get attention.

questions.question: Is hearing protection necessary when riding?

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed in addition to a helmet.
Only needed on windy days.
Not needed if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection lets you stay safe while still hearing horns and sirens.

questions.question: What is the best formation for group riding?

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving each rider enough space to stay safe. Use single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?

options.text: With the right hand
With the left hand
With the right foot
With the left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with the right hand.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on, but only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: Which provides the best face protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not adequate protection.
